# Game model (liquid-routing puzzle), 6 levels

## Board
- 512x512 = 16x16 blocks of 32px (fine grid is 64x64 cells of 8px; 4 cells = 1 block).
- Thin 8px GREEN line on one edge = move timer; depletes 16px per action → 32 actions per level.
- 1-block-thick GRAY strip on the opposite edge = the far wall / "escape" surface.
- SOURCE: a dark block + a magenta block (1 block wide). Liquid is emitted from the magenta
  cell travelling AWAY from the dark cell (dark is behind the nozzle). Source column/row fixed.
- CASTLE (yellow): 3 blocks wide x 2 tall "U"/"∩" with the middle block of the near row missing.
  That missing block is the NOTCH = target cup. Notch faces the incoming liquid.
- BARS: horizontal rectangles 1 block tall. BLUE = currently selected/controllable.
  RED = other bars (see selection below). Level 1 had one 5-wide bar; level 2 has
  one 5-wide blue + two 3-wide red.

## Actions
- ACTION1/2/3/4 = move the SELECTED (blue) bar up/down/left/right by 1 block.
- ACTION5 = run the liquid simulation. On failure the board reverts; on success level advances.
- ACTION6 = (testing) click a bar to select it.

## Liquid physics (deterministic)
- Liquid travels in a straight 1-block-wide stream from the source.
- When the stream is blocked by an obstacle at row r, it spreads horizontally along the
  adjacent row (r±1, the side it came from) from (obstacle_left − 1) to (obstacle_right + 1),
  then two new streams continue in the ORIGINAL direction at columns
  (obstacle_left − 1) and (obstacle_right + 1).
- Contiguous obstacle span in that row determines the ends (a castle leg alone = 1 block).

## Win condition (evidence)
- Level 1 FAILED when a stream reached the gray wall (turn 2: 1 escape; turn 5: 2 escapes,
  also wetted the yellow).
- Level 1 WON when both streams flowed straight into the two notches and nothing escaped.
- Working rule: EVERY stream must terminate inside a castle notch; nothing may reach the gray
  wall. Safest to also avoid touching yellow at all (enter each notch head-on).

## Visual tells during simulation
- Liquid = magenta. Wet yellow = dark maroon. Highlighted-but-dry yellow = white.
  Blue bar during sim = red. Gray wall turns green when liquid reaches it (= escape/failure).

# Liquid-routing puzzle — COMPLETED (6/6 levels)

## Board
- 512x512. Each level uses a uniform block size (32px in L1-3, 24px in L4-6).
  Derive it from the source block; playfield is inset by a gray border.
- Thin GREEN strip on one edge = move timer (depletes as actions are spent; budget is
  generous, ~100 actions in later levels). GRAY border = the wall; liquid reaching it = FAIL.

## Objects
- SOURCE: dark cap + magenta cell. Emits a 1-block stream travelling AWAY from the dark cap.
- BAR: 1-block-thick rectangle (horizontal or vertical). BLUE = currently selected; RED = not.
  A bar may contain a DARK cell = a second SOURCE built into the bar (emits in the level's
  global stream direction, moves with the bar). The bar is otherwise a solid obstacle.
- ELBOW (purple L, 3 cells: a 2-cell arm + 1 cell forming an L, i.e. a 2x2 square minus one
  corner). Movable. Acts as a 90-degree DEFLECTOR.
- CASTLE (yellow): 3x2 "U" with the middle cell of the outer row missing = the NOTCH (target
  cup). Castles may face any of the 4 directions (rotated 90 degrees for side/bottom walls).

## Actions
- ACTION6 <x,y>: click a piece to SELECT it (it turns blue). ACTION1/2/3/4 move the selected
  piece up/down/left/right by one block. Pieces cannot overlap, so plan movement paths.
- ACTION5: run the simulation. Success -> next level; failure -> board reverts unchanged.

## Physics (deterministic)
- A stream travels straight until blocked.
- BLOCKED BY A BAR/OBSTACLE: it spreads along the adjacent line it came from, from
  (contiguous_obstacle_start - 1) to (contiguous_obstacle_end + 1), then TWO new streams
  continue in the ORIGINAL direction at those two extreme positions.
  * Only the contiguous run of blocking cells counts (a castle leg alone = 1 cell).
  * A wall clips one side: a bar flush to a wall yields only ONE branch (no net split).
  * Cells in the spread line that are themselves blocked stop the spread on that side.
  * A vertical bar likewise splits a horizontal stream into two horizontal streams
    (offset one beyond each end) — the way to duplicate a sideways stream.
- ELBOW: deflects 90 degrees, but ONLY when the stream hits the far end of the arm that is
  perpendicular to its travel; it then turns toward the elbow's open side and continues along
  the line it was already in (it does NOT step into the elbow).
  Hitting the elbow's other arm-end just acts as a plain obstacle (and splits).
  Practically: place the arm so the stream passes under/beside the arm's far cell; the output
  line = the stream's current row/column.
- Streams may cross or merge harmlessly; two streams in the same lane are one.

## Win condition
Every stream must terminate inside a castle notch, entered head-on along the notch's axis;
all castles must be filled and nothing may reach the gray wall.
- Entering a notch is safe: the perpendicular spread is contained by the notch's own side legs.
- Counting rule: ends = (#sources) + (#splits). Elbows and wall-clipped bars add 0.
  Plan the split tree first; a split at a span [L,R] yields ends L-1 and R+1, so the
  distance between two notches fixes the required bar width (width = gap - 1).
  Duplicate entries into the same notch are allowed.

[After action · message]
**Game complete — WIN, 6/6 levels.**

Summary of how it went:

- **Level 1 (7 actions):** Discovered ACTION1–4 move a bar, ACTION5 runs a liquid simulation. Learned the core split rule (stream blocked → two streams at one block beyond each bar end) and solved it by spanning the bar so its edges lined up with the two castle notches.
- **Level 2 (8):** Found ACTION6 selects any bar. Chained two splits to fill three notches.
- **Level 3 (10):** Used wall-flush bars as *non-splitting* redirectors to merge branches, feeding three notches from three sources with zero escapes.
- **Level 4 (~28):** Discovered the dark cell inside a bar is a **second, movable source**. That re-framed the counting rule (ends = sources + splits) and made the 4-notch layout solvable.
- **Level 5 (~32, two probe runs):** Learned the purple L is a 90° deflector — and precisely *which* arm deflects vs. merely blocks. Two failed fires each pinpointed the exact rule, then a 1-block shift fixed it.
- **Level 6 (36):** Combined everything: a bar-nozzle straight into the bottom notch, one elbow turning a stream right into the side notch, the other turning a stream left, and a **vertical** bar splitting that sideways stream into two — filling all four notches on four different walls, first try.

The durable model is saved in `GUIDE.md`.
